lines.text: Six rooms, one guard, and a very sneaky thief. Every night, the guard misses him. Why?
The guard can watch only two rooms at once. A catch needs the right room, at the right time. Miss one, and the thief walks free.
The guard patrols the same route every night: rooms one, two, three, four. The thief notices, and always strikes the room the guard just left. Night after night, caught: zero.
Swap the museum for radio spectrum: rooms become frequency bands, the guard is the receiver, the thief is the emitter. Same trap, same blindness: detection, zero.

So we gave the guard a brain. Step one: a notebook. Which rooms get hit? Step two: a ranking. Check risky rooms first. Step three: dice. Mix up the patrol so it can't be predicted. Catches jump from zero point seven one zero, to zero point nine six seven.
This is the real product. Press run the demo: the dashboard streams a live simulation, the waterfall, the policies racing, and Index pulling ahead on the same seed.
Pushpak. The guard that learned where to look. Simulation only.
